reference: Poisot et al. The dissimilarity of species interaction networks. Ecology Letters 2012
boundary_for_new_program: Already provides network dissimilarity across space/time/environment and separates species turnover from interaction change; do not claim invention of interaction beta diversity.

reference: Fründ. Dissimilarity of species interaction networks: how to partition rewiring and species turnover components. Ecosphere 2021
boundary_for_new_program: Provides explicit rewiring/species-turnover partitions including additive common-denominator implementation; new contribution must be cross-axis biological prediction, not decomposition itself.

reference: Rohr & Bascompte. Components of phylogenetic signal in antagonistic and mutualistic networks. American Naturalist 2014
boundary_for_new_program: Phylogenetic constraints in network architecture and differences among interaction types are prior art; interaction-time response is not itself novel.

reference: Trait-based inference of ecological network assembly: a conceptual framework and methodological toolbox. Ecological Monographs 2022
boundary_for_new_program: Trait-based network assembly is prior art; novelty requires the common time-space turnover question and paired predictor effects.

reference: Ward et al. The rewiring of ecological networks in a variable world. Nature Reviews Biodiversity 2026
boundary_for_new_program: Rewiring as dynamic response to environmental variation and trait-mediated mechanisms is prior art; do not claim first recognition that networks rewire.

reference: McLeod et al. Effects of species traits, motif profiles, and environment on spatial variation in multi-trophic antagonistic networks. Ecosphere 2020
boundary_for_new_program: Traits and environment predicting spatial network turnover are prior art; new question is whether the same predictor structure also explains evolutionary-time turnover.
